ch15.d.A: Distance $A$ the block is pulled from equilibrium before release
ch15.d.k: Stiffness $k$ of the spring; larger means more force for the same displacement
ch15.d.m: Mass $m$ of the block on the spring
ch15.d.damp: Strength of a drag force proportional to velocity; 0 means no damping
ch15.d.vectors: $\vec v$ and $\vec a$ of the point on the circle, and $v$, $a$ of the block (vertical parts)
ch15.goal.proj: Simple harmonic motion = the projection of uniform circular motion onto one axis
ch15.goal.props: Properties of a harmonic oscillator: the period does not depend on the amplitude, $\omega = \sqrt{k/m}$, $K + U$ is constant
ch15.obs.phase: Graphs: $v$ leads $x$ by $90^\circ$; the speed is largest at $x = 0$ and $v = 0$ at the turning points
ch15.obs.a: The $a$ graph is the $x$ graph flipped and scaled by $\omega^2$ ($a = -\omega^2 x$): the vertical part of the centripetal acceleration on the circle
ch15.obs.iso: Amplitude 0.1 m → 0.3 m: the period $T$ stays the same (isochronism)
ch15.obs.km: $k$ times 4 or $m$ divided by 4: $\omega$ doubles, the period halves
ch15.obs.energy: Energy graph: $K$ and $U$ trade every half period; their sum $E = \tfrac{1}{2}kA^2$ stays constant
ch15.obs.damp: Damping ratio 0.05: the amplitude and $E$ decay exponentially; the period barely changes
ch15.assume.spring: Ideal massless spring; $x$ is the displacement from equilibrium (gravity only shifts the equilibrium). Free-body diagram: the hanging spring pulls with $F_s = mg - kx$, $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$
ch15.assume.scale: Arrows on the circle: $v$ scaled by $1/\omega$, $a$ by $1/\omega^2$
ch15.assume.zeta: Damping ratio $\zeta = b/(2\sqrt{km})$, where $b$ is the damping constant of the damping force $F_d = -bv$. $\zeta < 1$ underdamped, $\zeta = 1$ critically damped, $\zeta > 1$ overdamped (this scene: $\zeta \le 0.2$, underdamped only). Link to the symbols of the review page Damped Oscillations: $\gamma = b/2m = \zeta\omega_0$, $b_c = 2\sqrt{km}$, so $\zeta = b/b_c$
ch15.assume.damp: With damping, $\omega$ and $T$ in the readouts belong to the damped oscillation: $\omega = \omega_0\sqrt{1 - \zeta^2}$, $T = 2\pi/\omega$, $\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m}$
ch15.n.d.theta0: Angle $\theta_0$ from the vertical at release
ch15.n.d.L: Distance $L$ from the pivot to the centre of the bob
ch15.n.goal.small: Small angles: $\sin\theta \approx \theta$, so the motion is SHM with period $T_0 = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$
ch15.n.goal.large: Large angles: the restoring force grows more slowly than $\theta$, so the period is longer and depends on the amplitude
ch15.n.obs.L: Four times the length: twice the period, the same error
ch15.n.assume: Massless string (a massless rod beyond 90°), point bob, no air resistance, $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$. Drawn scaled to $L$, so every length looks the same. Free-body diagram for a 1 kg bob (the motion does not depend on the mass)
ch15.n.d.vectors: $\vec v$ of the bob and its acceleration in two parts: tangential $a_\text{t}$ and radial $a_\text{r}$ (towards the pivot)
ch15.n.obs.err: Error of the small-angle model, $(T - T_0)/T_0$: 0.19 % at 10°, 1.7 % at 30°, 18 % at 90°, 76 % at 150°
ch15.n.obs.arrows: Arrows: at the turning points $v = 0$ and $a_\text{t}$ is largest; at the bottom $v$ is largest, $a_\text{t} = 0$ and $a_\text{r} = v^2/L$ is largest
ch15.n.obs.graph: $\theta$ graph, grey dashed: the small-angle model $\theta_0\cos\omega_0 t$ ($\omega_0 = \sqrt{g/L}$); at 90° the real pendulum falls further behind each swing
ch15.n.obs.at: Formula panel: real $a_\text{t} = -g\sin\theta$ against the model $a_{\text{t},0} = -g\theta$. At large $\theta$ the model overestimates the restoring acceleration, so its period is shorter
ch15.n.assume.err: $T$: period of the real motion (exact, $K$ = complete elliptic integral of the first kind); the simulation (RK4) returns to $\theta_0$ after $T$. The error compares $T$ with the model $T_0$, relative to $T_0$
ch15.n.assume.arrows: Arrow lengths: $v$ and the acceleration parts are each scaled so that their largest value in the swing has the same length; $a_\text{t}$ and $a_\text{r}$ share one scale. $a_\text{t}$ is drawn just outside $v$ on the same line
ch15.n.obs.inset: Graph below the pendulum: the period error $\Delta T/T_0 = (T - T_0)/T_0$ against the release angle $\theta_0$ (log scale), the black dot at the current angle. The smaller the angle, the faster the error falls, as $\theta_0^2/16$: below 1 % (grey dashed line) under 23°, 0.19 % at 10°
